subject.title: Per-account native command prefix for multi-agent slash commands

question: Should Slack multi-account native slash commands be solved with validated account-level nativeNames mapping, constrained nativePrefix sugar, or documented as unsupported for duplicate native command names?
rationale: Current main has no account-level naming contract, and the two prior unmerged PRs show a real design fork between prefix convenience and explicit mappings; either implementation adds user-visible Slack config/API surface.

options.title: Implement Validated nativeNames
options.body: Add explicit per-account native command mapping with duplicate and Slack-format validation, registration, reverse lookup, arg-menu callback support, docs, and focused tests.

options.title: Implement Constrained nativePrefix
options.body: Add prefix sugar only with strict lowercase slug validation and no broad dash-stripping fallback, accepting a simpler UX but a second naming abstraction.

options.title: Document Unsupported Duplicate Names
options.body: Leave runtime unchanged and document that multiple Slack apps in one workspace must not register identical native command names, preserving the current config surface at the cost of this workflow.

recommendation.title: Implement Validated nativeNames
recommendation.body: Add explicit per-account native command mapping with duplicate and Slack-format validation, registration, reverse lookup, arg-menu callback support, docs, and focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal on the shared native command registry and Slack provider override behavior that this product contract would change.
